Quote verbatim in abstract; abstract also confirms HBsAg/HBeAg fell only with peg-IFN and cccDNA did not differ between groups, as the judgement says.

Quote verbatim in PMC7577125 (two citations follow 'clinical studies'). Meets rules 1-2 literally, but model-side evidence is 'data not shown' and sponsor-authored; recommend confidence low. NCT02908191 has no posted results, so null is correct.

24-word clause verified; host sentence (44 words) only records a precautionary stop amid a host-flare hypothesis. Contra rests on the HS follow-up ('AB-506 hepatotoxicity contributed') and programme termination, both verified. GLS4/JNJ-6379 are not named in the paper.

missing: efficacy, candidate 2024 contra (or at least a flagged entry): Yuen 2024 JHEP Rep, doi 10.1016/j.jhepr.2023.100999 (PMC10951643, read in full). Discussion puts vebicorvir trough concentrations 'above the protein-adjusted EC50 (paEC50) values for HBV DNA and cccDNA formation' beside 'we conclude that long-term treatment with VBR + NrtI does not result in functional cure' and attributes failure to 'the inability of current treatment regimens to interfere with cccDNA formation and maintenance'. That is a published comparison of the Huang 2020 cell-culture secondary-MoA prediction (cccDNA formation blocked) with patients. Source frames it as scaling (next-generation potency needed), not a miss. Note Huang 2020 has no in-vivo efficacy model: for vebicorvir the efficacy model WAS cell culture, so 'best model' differs by drug within the class.

dose, candidate 2024 entry from the same Yuen 2024 sentence: a published patient-trough vs in-vitro paEC50 statement for vebicorvir (target met for HBV DNA and cccDNA formation). Would extend the dose strip past 2021.
dose 2019: Lam 2019 cites the patient trough confirmation as unpublished; Yuen 2019 Gastroenterology (doi 10.1053/j.gastro.2018.12.023, paywalled) may contain it. Unverified; the abstract does not.

registry_date checks: NCT02401737 (NVR 3-778 phase 1b) and NCT02908191 (ABI-H0731 phase 1a/1b) have no results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov, so null is correct. NCT02112799 (NVR 3-778 part 1) and the vebicorvir phase 2a records NCT03576066 / NCT03577171 were not checked. AB-506-001/-003 have no ClinicalTrials.gov record (sponsor search returns only AB-101) and Yuen 2022 gives no registry ID. Zhang 2021 is CTR20160068 on chinadrugtrials.org.cn.
rule_questions: Direction-only match from a sponsor sentence: rules give efficacy/engagement 2019 'same' because Lam 2019 states the comparison and calls it a match, while the magnitude miss (mono NVR 3-778 ~ entecavir in mice; 1.43 log10 in 4 weeks in patients) can only be built by the drafter from other primary sources, which rule 1 does not allow to drive 'contra'. Should magnitude='direction_only' + source_calls_it='match' + sponsor authorship cap confidence, or does the atlas want a status that distinguishes direction-only matches from quantitative ones?

Model-side evidence 'data not shown': safety 2020 'same' rests on Huang 2020's one sentence asserting a clean toxicology panel with no data. Rule 1 asks for a primary source making the comparison, not for the model result to be reported anywhere. Decide whether an unreported model result counts (then confidence low) or whether the status should fall to 'untested'.

Two models used by the same class for the same question disagree: the humanized mouse predicted no cccDNA/antigen effect (matched the clinic); the cell-culture cccDNA-formation assay used for vebicorvir predicted a secondary MoA that did not translate (Yuen 2024). 'Best model' = the one relied on, but reliance split by sponsor. Does the cell-culture miss score 'contra' for the context even though the mouse was right, and when the source calls it 'scaling'?

Quote as a clause: safety 2022 quotes 24 words of a 44-word sentence whose own framing is a precautionary stop inside a host-flare hypothesis; the miss is closed by a different sentence in the same paper. Rule 2 says 'the sentence'. Allow clause quotes when the host sentence exceeds 40 words, provided the judgement cites the sentence that closes the comparison?
